learningObjective: Trace how moving one speaker-verification threshold changes false rejects and false accepts on the same set of target and non-target trials.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can hold trial scores fixed while moving only the decision boundary, making the operating-point tradeoff causal rather than merely verbal. Direct labels and repeated geometry keep the comparison readable without interaction or color.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a flowchart can show enrollment and scoring stages, but automatic layout cannot preserve a shared score axis or demonstrate which fixed trials cross a moved threshold.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: deterministic coordinates place the same target and non-target trials on aligned score strips, so changing only the threshold visibly changes the two error types.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table could list decisions at two thresholds, but readers would still need to reconstruct score order, boundary movement, and the traded errors.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: a threshold slider could expose more operating points, but adds controls and hidden states when two static, aligned examples establish the intended inference.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: authoritative sources define detection errors, costs, and calibration, but no permissive license to adapt their figures was established. The shipped visual uses original geometry, labels, and illustrative trial positions.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose says thresholds depend on risk but does not let a reader hold scores constant and see why reducing false rejects necessarily risks accepting more non-target trials.

pages.insight: The Automatic Speech Recognition divider begins the deck's only contiguous speech-focused section; it concerns transcription rather than speaker identity.
The Speech recognition title slide contains no speaker verification, enrollment, similarity score, or decision threshold.
The slide contrasts end-to-end and traditional speech-to-text pipelines and therefore helps distinguish word recognition from the identity decision discussed in this article.
The slide defines waveform-to-text recognition and lists acoustic, pronunciation, and language-model components, none of which supplies a speaker-verification operating-point model.
The RNN-T slide closes the speech section with transcription and prediction networks; it does not address speaker embeddings, target versus non-target trials, or verification thresholds.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-4 (GPT-5.6 Sol) text-indexed all 214 physical PDF pages for speaker, voiceprint, verification, identification, impostor, enrollment, and threshold. No speaker-recognition slide or relevant figure was found. Pages 119-126 were then reviewed as the complete contiguous speech neighborhood. Neighboring page 118 is knowledge-graph embeddings and page 127 begins model compression, confirming the topic boundary. No deck image, wording, numerical value, or layout is reused.

sources.license: The NIST page is publicly accessible, but no figure is reused or adapted. The visual contains no NIST data, benchmark result, wording, or layout.

sources.title: X-Vectors: Robust DNN Embeddings for Speaker Recognition
sources.usage: Used as a primary source to verify fixed-dimensional neural speaker embeddings and their use with a scoring backend for text-independent speaker recognition.
sources.license: The author-hosted paper is publicly readable, but no permissive figure-adaptation license was identified. No figure, architecture, experiment, value, wording, or layout is reused.

sources.title: Application-independent evaluation of speaker detection
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for the distinction between application-independent speaker-detector scores and application-dependent Bayesian decisions, including calibration across operating costs and priors.
sources.license: The publisher page does not grant permission to adapt the paper's figures. The visual is an original qualitative score strip and copies no figure, data, equation, wording, or layout.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is the operating-point tradeoff after scoring: the embedding and backend produce an ordered match score, but the application chooses a threshold, and moving that single boundary changes both false-reject and false-accept exposure. The two rows deliberately reuse identical, invented trial positions; only the threshold moves. They make no empirical claim about score distributions, EER, calibration quality, or any deployed system.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, indexed the full 214-page deck and inspected its contiguous speech neighborhood, then checked official NIST material and primary speaker-embedding and calibration papers before selecting an original threshold tradeoff schematic.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and complete description. Target trials are circles labeled T, non-target trials are squares labeled N, thresholds are vertical boundary lines, and each error is directly bracketed and named, so color is redundant. The 360-unit viewBox scales without a fixed or minimum width for a 390 CSS-pixel viewport. Existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, shared print rules force a light high-contrast palette, and the established visual-scroll wrapper prevents clipping.
